newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly up on USDA acreage estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly up on USDA acreage estimate.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly higher on bullish input from USDA's estimate for 1997 U.S. winter wheat acreage, traders said.
"The second biggest surprise in the report was the wheat acreage number. That's a tremendous drop, the three million acres," said Paul Haugens, vice president for FIMAT Futures.
USDA said U.S. farmers last fall seeded 48.222 million acres of winter wheat, well below an average of analysts' estimates for 51.4 million acres.

Gains in wheat were trimmed by commercial selling with Cargill Inc a key seller of four million bushels of the March, traders said. Wheat spreads were featured with the nearby March ending lower as USDA increased to 469 million from the previous 435 million its outlook for U.S. wheat ending stocks.
Wheat closed 10 cents per bushel higher to 2-1/4 lower, with March down 2-1/4 at $3.87. July was up 8-1/2 cents at $3.54-1/4.
Some traders cited cold weather in the U.S. winter wheat region as supportive to wheat futures but many said the snowfall this week will help insulate the crop from damage.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, above the 12,963 contracts traded Thursday.

In wheat options, Prudential Securities sold 300 May $3.80 calls at 15 to 15-1/2 cents, Smith Barney bought 200 July $3.60 puts at 22-1/2 cents and Prudential sold 400 July $4.00 calls at 8-1/2 to 9-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, above the 5,339 contracts traded Thursday.
